claim: MOH's Expatriate Labor Screening Unit tests expatriates for hepatitis B and C, HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis, and gives vaccinations including meningitis
quote: conducting medical tests to detect infectious diseases, such as hepatitis B and C, HIV/AIDS, and tuberculosis. Additionally, the unit ensures that expatriates receive necessary vaccinations, including meningitis vaccines

claim: Results of the expatriate medical are recorded electronically in the Ministry of Interior's system to speed up the residency process
quote: Examination results are electronically recorded in the Ministry of Interior’s system to facilitate the monitoring of expatriates' health and expedite the residency process.

claim: MOH runs five main labour screening centres: Shuwaikh Main Center, Fahaheel, Rumaithiya, Jahra and Subhan, open Sunday to Thursday 7:30 am to 6 pm
quote: namely: Shuwaikh Main Center, Fahaheel Center, Rumaithiya Center, Jahra Center, and Subhan Center. These centers are open from Sunday to Thursday, 7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

claim: When an infectious disease is found, re-examinations confirm it; cases posing a significant public health threat are removed (deported), treatable cases are referred to specialised centres
quote: When cases of infectious diseases are identified, re-examinations are conducted to confirm diagnoses, and appropriate measures are taken. Cases that pose a significant public health threat are removed, while treatable cases are referred to specialized medical centers.

claim: The most common diseases found in the expatriate screening are tuberculosis, hepatitis B and C, and HIV/AIDS
quote: He highlighted that the most common diseases detected during these screenings are tuberculosis, hepatitis B and C, and HIV/AIDS.

claim: Except domestic workers with their sponsor present, applicants need a prior appointment at the expatriate labour examination centres
quote: domestic workers can undergo examinations without prior appointments in all expatriate labor examination centers, provided their sponsor is present. For other applicants, securing a prior appointment is a prerequisite.

claim: MOH expat examination centres include Ali Sabah Al-Salem (Umm Al-Hayman), Al-Jahra and Shuwaikh
quote: three expat examination centers: the centers in Ali Sabah Al-Salem suburb (Umm Al-Hayman), Al-Jahra, and Shuwaikh

claim: Workers are examined abroad at accredited centres, approved by Kuwaiti embassies as part of the visa process, and examined again on arrival to get the health certificate needed for residency
quote: Expatriates seeking to work in the country must undergo medical examinations at accredited centers abroad, which are then approved by Kuwaiti consulates or embassies as part of the visa application process.

claim: The arrival medical covers HIV, hepatitis B and C, tuberculosis and, depending on the country of origin, malaria and filariasis
quote: The tests cover not only HIV but also other diseases such as hepatitis B and C, tuberculosis, and additional illnesses depending on the traveler’s country of origin, including malaria and filariasis.

claim: Food handlers, barbers, health-centre staff and similar jobs face periodic medical examinations
quote: Certain job categories, especially those involved in food handling, barbershops, health centers, and other sectors with specific health requirements, are subject to periodic medical examinations.

claim: Since a May 2025 directive, residency applicants and new arrivals with an 'indeterminate' HIV antibody result are classed medically unfit and barred
quote: has issued a directive barring residency applicants and new arrivals from entering the country if their HIV antibody test results are deemed “indeterminate.” Such individuals will be classified as medically unfit.

claim: Similar rules already applied to indeterminate hepatitis C results
quote: following similar guidelines for indeterminate Hepatitis C cases

claim: MOH (2018): workers are re-tested right after arrival; anyone found with a listed disease is deported and put on the banned list
quote: وتتم إعادة إجراء الفحوصات الطبية عليه داخل الكويت عقب وصوله إلى البلاد مباشرة، وفي حال اكتشاف إصابته بأي مرض يبعد ويدرج اسمه ضمن قوائم المحظورين

claim: On arrival in GCC states, workers get fresh tests focused on infectious diseases; the Wafid pre-departure check covers some 50 tests
quote: Those centers are required to carry out some 50 medical tests on expats, including infectious and non-infectious diseases. When they arrive in GCC nations, the workers are subjected to fresh tests focusing on infectious diseases.

claim: The updated Wafid resolution, effective 17 May 2026, covers fees paid by applicants and attestation of results by GCC missions abroad
quote: fees to be paid by applicants and the attestation of results by GCC missions abroad

claim: From 10 March 2019 new residence permits come on the Civil ID card instead of a residence sticker in the passport
quote: foreign nationals who applied for residence permits in Kuwait on or after March 10, 2019 will receive the new Civil Identification card instead of a residence sticker when applying for initial or renewed permits.

claim: The Civil ID shows the passport number and profession and is needed to enter or leave Kuwait
quote: The new Civil Identification card includes the foreign national’s passport number and profession and is required to enter or depart Kuwait

claim: After post-arrival registration, the sponsor requests the Civil ID through PACI's online portal
quote: upon completing post-arrival registration procedures, the sponsoring entity requests a Civil Identification card for the applicant through the PACI’s online portal.

claim: Names and details on the Civil ID must match the passport, or the holder may be refused entry or exit; Arabic-to-Latin transliteration caused mismatches
quote: should ensure that their personal information printed in their new Civil Identification card matches the details in their passports in order to avoid being denied entry or departure from Kuwait.

claim: A worker can get his Civil ID number from the company HR department
quote: If you are on a work visa, you can also enquire about your Civil ID number with your company’s human resources (HR) department.

claim: Card status: services.paci.gov.kw/card/inquiry, Card Status, enter the Civil ID number; when ready it shows the collection location
quote: If it is ready, you will receive the message that the card is ready for collection, along with the location of the centre from where you can collect it.

claim: PACI's hotline for Civil ID status is 188988
quote: You can also call the PACI helpline – 188988 – to get an update on your card’s status.

claim: While waiting for the card, the digital Civil ID can be set up in the Kuwait Mobile ID app
quote: even as you wait for the Civil ID card to be delivered to you, you can get the digital version of your Civil ID through the ‘Kuwait Mobile ID’ app

claim: Kuwait Mobile ID registration asks for the Civil ID number and passport number, then email and mobile number
quote: You will then be asked to enter your Civil ID number and passport number.

claim: Kuwait Mobile ID registration takes a face photo, sends an OTP to the mobile, and asks for a 4- to 12-digit PIN
quote: The PIN number has to be between four to 12 digits, and the numbers cannot be serialised or duplicated.

claim: Kuwait Mobile ID: take a face photo with the front camera; after verification an OTP is sent to the registered mobile
quote: Once the image is successfully verified, you will receive a one-time password (OTP) on your registered mobile number.

claim: Civil ID fee is KD 5 (raised from KD 2 in 2016); reissue for loss or damage KD 20; payable online on PACI's website
quote: the fee would be KD 5 instead of KD 2.

claim: Reissue of a lost or damaged Civil ID costs KD 20; fees can be paid online on PACI's website
quote: increasing the fees re-issue in cases of loss or damage from KD 10 to 20. The civil ID fees could be paid online at the PACI’s website.

claim: Optional home delivery of the Civil ID costs KD 2 on top of the KD 5 card fee (KD 7 in all)
quote: the recipient will have to pay KD 7 (KD 5 the charge of the Civil ID).

claim: Civil IDs are handed out by vending machines, 9 am to 8 pm, and must be collected within 3 months
quote: On a daily basis 10,000 to 13,000 civil id cards are issued through vending machines between 9am to 8 pm.

claim: Civil ID cards must be collected within 3 months
quote: Civil id cards need to be collected within a period of 3 months.

claim: Over 200,000 uncollected cards sat in the South Surra machines, more than 90% of them Article 18 expatriates'
quote: More than 200,000 cards have not been collected over 3 months from the machines in South Surra reports al qabas.

claim: More than 90% of uncollected Civil IDs in the machines belong to Article 18 expatriates
quote: More than 90% of civil id cards lying in  vending machines are of expats who are on Article 18.

claim: In January 2025 the Central Bank of Kuwait directed banks to open accounts for all, including low-income, service and craft workers and domestic workers, without a minimum salary
quote: The Central Bank of Kuwait has directed banks to begin opening bank accounts for all customer categories, including those with limited or low incomes, job holders, workers in simple service and craft jobs, and domestic workers.

claim: Banks may not refuse an account on the basis of salary or income
quote: ensure that banks do not refuse to open accounts based on salary or income level

claim: Banks must open these 'worker accounts' on request but will not market them
quote: while banks must comply with these directives and open these accounts upon request, they will not actively market them

claim: ABK's Al Amel is a labour salary account for company workers earning less than KD 300, expatriates only
quote: Salaries of less than KD 300

claim: Only expatriates may open an ABK Al Amel account
quote: Only expatriate customers may open an Al Amel account

claim: ABK has dedicated Al Amel branches in Sabhan and Salmiya
quote: Dedicated branches in Sabhan and Salmiya for Al Amel laborers

claim: Al Amel needs a letter from the company to open the account
quote: Letter from company or establishment to open an Al Amel account

claim: Al Amel also needs the company's commercial licence and signature authorisation
quote: Company Commercial License and Signature Authorization

claim: Al Amel needs a copy of a valid Civil ID, the passport (with the address page) and the work permit
quote: Copy of valid civil ID and passport copy including the address page and work permit

claim: Al Amel gives free monthly statements and a free debit card for 5 years
quote: Free debit card issue/renewal for 5 years

claim: Al Amel does not accept salary transfers from other banks
quote: Salary transfers from other banks are not allowed

claim: Burgan Bank's Al Rateb salary account needs a salary of at least KD 400 for expatriates
quote: expats with a minimum salary of KD 400.

claim: Bank loans to expatriates start at a salary of KD 600
quote: customers earning 600 dinars or more can access loans up to 15,000 dinars

claim: Residents register a SIM with their Civil ID; visitors with a passport
quote: Residents need to show their Civil ID (or “Bataka”) to register a SIM card.

claim: Visitors register a SIM with a valid original passport
quote: A valid passport (not a photocopy)

claim: SIM registration in Kuwait is governed by strict rules; operators must verify each new customer's identity
quote: Telecom providers must ensure that every new customer identity is verified accurately

claim: A worker who arrived at Kuwait Oil Al Naseef Company through a Bangladeshi agency was told on arrival his visa was fake and he still owed money for it, or would be sent home
quote: when I arrived, the company's office told me my visa was fake. They said I still owed money for the visa and should ask the broker to pay the remaining amount, or I'd be sent back home

claim: The Kuwait Embassy in Dhaka gave TBS only an email address for queries and did not answer by 28 February 2025
quote: However, despite sending the queries on the same day, there was no response from the embassy as of 28 February 2025.

claim: Kuwait is the main destination for Bangladeshi nurses
quote: Bangladesh is currently sending nurses mainly to Kuwait, which has emerged as one of the largest overseas employers of the former's nurses in recent years.

claim: In October 2025 Kuwait sought 100 nurses from Bangladesh through BOESL
quote: In October 2025, Kuwait sought to recruit 100 nurses from Bangladesh through Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Limited (BOESL).

claim: Candidates needed English, at least 3 years' experience, technical skills and basic life support certification
quote: Candidates were required to demonstrate English proficiency, at least three years of work experience, relevant technical skills and certification in basic life support.

claim: Offered salaries: up to Tk 1.27 lakh for BSc nurses and Tk 1.11 lakh for diploma nurses
quote: The offered salaries reached Tk1.27 lakh for BSc nurses and Tk1.11 lakh for diploma nurses.

claim: Of 100 who sat the recruitment exam, 15 were selected
quote: Although 100 candidates sat for the recruitment examination, only 15 were ultimately selected, according to BOESL.

claim: By May 2026 only five had completed visa processing
quote: said only five nurses have so far completed visa processing.

claim: BOESL says Kuwaiti authorities had not granted clearance for the nurses because of Middle East tensions
quote: Due to the ongoing tensions in the Middle East, the Kuwaiti authorities have not yet granted emigration clearance for the nurses

claim: By end-2024, 677 Bangladeshi nurses had been placed in Kuwaiti public hospitals since structured deployment began in 2022 (BOESL Annual Report 2023-24)
quote: By the end of 2024, a total of 677 Bangladeshi nurses had been placed in Kuwaiti public hospitals, according to the BOESL Annual Report 2023–24.

claim: In May 2023 the Bangladesh Embassy in Kuwait signed an MoU with Kuwait's health ministry on recruiting medical professionals (G2G)
quote: the Bangladesh Embassy in Kuwait City signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the health ministry of Kuwait last month.

claim: City Group General Trading Company and Advanced Technology Company, with MOH approval, sought 998 nurses through BOESL in December 2021
quote: the City Group General Trading Company and the Advanced Technology Company of Kuwait submitted demand letters to the Embassy on December 2021 for recruitment of 998 nurses through Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Limited (BOESL)

claim: A selection committee of Kuwait MOH and the companies selected 654 nurses in Bangladesh in January 2022
quote: a selection committee comprising of the Ministry of Health, Kuwait and representatives from respective company visited Bangladesh to recruit nurses for both of the companies and finalized a total number of 654 nurses.

claim: The first 50 nurses arrived in June 2022 for MOH government hospitals, officially free of cost
quote: 50 nurses of the first batch have arrived in Kuwait for the first time officially free of cost.

claim: BOESL nurses (2022) went without migration cost; salary Tk 80,000-90,000 a month with overtime and yearly increment
quote: The monthly salary is varying from Tk 80,000 to Tk 90,000 with overtime and a yearly increment.

claim: The 2022 BOESL nurses were recruited without migration cost through City Group General Trading and Advance Technology Company
quote: The professionals are being recruited without migration cost through City Group General Trading Company and Advance Technology Company in Kuwait.

claim: Dataflow primary source verification of credentials is mandatory for the Kuwait MOH licence
quote: Submit credentials through Dataflow for the Kuwait MOH pathway - mandatory and cannot be waived.

claim: The employer submits the licence application with the Dataflow report on MOH's portal; fees are paid online
quote: Your employer submits the formal licence application with your Dataflow report and all supporting documents. Fees are paid online.

claim: MOH then sends exam eligibility; the candidate sits a computer-based Prometric exam, results go to MOH
quote: Register with Prometric, select a test centre (international centres available for most professions), and sit the written exam.

claim: Nurses need 3 years' experience, now in an acute inpatient setting
quote: Nurses remain at 3 years but experience must now be in an acute inpatient setting

claim: Documents include a good standing certificate within 6 months, the Dataflow receipt, a criminal background check and vaccination records
quote: a good standing certificate (within 6 months), Dataflow receipt, criminal background check, vaccination records, and passport copies

claim: kuwaitvisa.moi.gov.kw handles tourist, family, business and government visit visas; residency or work permit status is checked separately
quote: If you hold a Kuwait residency or work permit, that status is checked separately

claim: The MOI portal kuwaitvisa.moi.gov.kw handles visit visas (tourist, family, business, government)
quote: which now handles tourist, family, business, and government visit visas

claim: Kuwait Mobile ID: download from Apple App Store, Google Play or Huawei AppGallery
quote: Download the app from Apple App Store, Google Play or Huawei AppGallery.

claim: Kuwait Mobile ID: tap 'Get started' then 'registration'
quote: Tap on ‘Get started’ and then on ‘registration’.

claim: Kuwait Mobile ID: choose 'enter data manually' instead of reading the card by NFC
quote: Choose the option ‘enter data manually’.

claim: Kuwait Mobile ID: enter email address and mobile number, then 'next'
quote: Next, enter your email address and mobile number and click on ‘next’.

claim: Civil ID status page: click 'Card Status', enter the Civil ID number, submit
quote: Click on ‘Card Status’.
